The new generation Mac mini equipped with M6 and M5 Pro chips officially launched this week, but afterwards we discovered three details that Apple did not specifically mention during the announcement.

#1: Memory bandwidth varies across different configurations

If you plan to order the Mac mini, the pre-order page actually does not fully list the key specification of memory bandwidth. Looking into the technical details reveals that the choice of RAM directly affects the overall memory bandwidth.

The base model Mac mini with the M6 chip comes with 16GB of RAM, providing 153GB/s memory bandwidth; however, if you upgrade to 24GB or 32GB of RAM, the bandwidth increases to 170GB/s.

On the other hand, to achieve the highest memory bandwidth of 307GB/s, you need to choose the M5 Pro chip.

Each configuration still represents an improvement compared to the M4 model, but the differences are worth noting.

#2: N1 chip brings Thread support

When Apple announced the new Mac mini, it highlighted support for Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, both upgrades compared to the M4 model's Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.3.

However, looking into the technical specifications reveals that the M6 Mac mini includes an Apple-designed N1 chip, allowing the Mac mini to simultaneously support the Thread protocol.

Thread has been included in iPhones since the iPhone 15 Pro, and Apple has consistently emphasised its benefits for smart home accessories and automation. However, this is the first time it has been added to the Mac mini.

#3: Pre-installed with macOS Golden Gate

If you prefer to wait before upgrading to the new macOS, note that the M6 Mac mini comes pre-installed with macOS Golden Gate out of the box.

Apple did not explicitly mention this on its official website, but according to reports, the company has confirmed to John Gruber that the new version of macOS is the pre-installed system.

This is actually not surprising, as the M6 Mac mini will not officially ship until September 22, while macOS 27 is expected to launch the week before (around September 14 or thereabouts). Still, users who have reservations about upgrading to the latest system should take note.

To learn about a full comparison between the M6 Mac mini and the M4 model, you can check out our overview article.

Starting from US$899, you can pre-order the Mac mini equipped with M6 and M5 Pro right now.

Would you consider buying the M6 Mac mini? What are your reasons? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
